You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" *

Adds all the elements of the given arrays into a new array.

*

The new array contains all of the element of array1 followed * by all of the elements array2. When an array is returned, it is always * a new array.

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, null)     = null
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(array1, null)   = cloned copy of array1
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, array2)   = cloned copy of array2
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([], [])         = []
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([null], [null]) = [null, null]
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(["a", "b", "c"], ["1", "2", "3"]) = ["a", "b", "c", "1", "2", "3"]
     *
* * @param array1 the first array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @param array2 the second array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @return The new array, null if both arrays are null. * The type of the new array is the type of the first array, * unless the first array is null, in which case the type is the same as the second array. * @since 2.1 "

Diagnosis:
The test failure and bug report reveal an issue in the method ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2). The test tries to add all elements of an Integer array and a Long array into a Number array, which works fine, but when trying to add a Long array to an Integer array, it throws an ArrayStoreException at System.arraycopy.

The addAll method creates a new array of the type of the first input array (array1) using reflection (Array.newInstance(type1, ...)) and then attempts to copy the contents of array1 and array2 into this new array using System.arraycopy. The problem arises during the second copy (array2) when array2 contains elements that are not compatible with the first array type (type1).

Since the new array is of the component type of array1, trying to copy elements from array2, which may have a different component type (e.g., Long for an Integer array1), results in an ArrayStoreException. The method does not check if array2 elements are compatible with array1's component type before copying.

The bug report recommends that instead of the less obvious ArrayStoreException, a clear IllegalArgumentException should be thrown for incompatible array types in addAll. This would require additional compatibility checks before the System.arraycopy call of array2 elements.

The root cause is that the addAll method does not verify the component type compatibility of array2 against array1 before creating and copying into the new array. It blindly assumes both arrays contain compatible element types, leading to runtime exceptions for mixed incompatible types.

No useful info was found in recent unrelated bug reports.

Summary:
- addAll constructs a new array of array1's component type,
- It then copies array1 and array2 content into this array,
- If array2's component type elements are not assignable to array1's component type, an ArrayStoreException occurs,
- No explicit compatibility check is performed before copying array2,
- The test expects an IllegalArgumentException for incompatible types but instead ArrayStoreException is thrown,
- The code should be fixed to detect incompatibilities and throw a clearer exception before the copy.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
